blocking_changes_before_AB06_pilot: B1: census self-count (gap 1). Apply the one-line diff or the in-module override, add a real-census test, rebind.

B2: orphaned MATLAB. The watch loop roots the tree at the recorded PID and ends as soon as that PID has no row. If bin\matlab.exe is only a stub that starts the real MATLAB and exits, the tree is empty at the first poll, the job is reported 'completed' while MATLAB runs unwatched and un-killable by this code; the post-run census would only flag it afterwards. I could not confirm which behaviour R2023b has without running MATLAB. Minimal safe change: after the root PID has no row, query Windows processes whose command line contains the run nonce and whose name starts with 'matlab'; if one exists, adopt its PID and creation time as the recorded identity (written into the receipt) and keep watching and stopping it; if the tree is gone and outputs are missing within the first poll, mark the run failed rather than completed. Add a fake-host test for this. A supervised pilot would settle the real behaviour.
non_blocking_recommendations: Constrain source_root to the two reviewed roots (repo CAMARGO folder, gt21_author_mirror_2024_extracted) and output_root to converted_datasets/reconversion_v2/ in validate_native_spec.
If start_matlab raises after the process started, no identity exists and MATLAB could run unwatched; on exception also run the nonce query from B2.

The Windows after-run census flags any new process whose name starts with 'matlab' (for example MathWorks helper services), so a healthy run can still show windows_no_new_worker false. The pilot should list them; decide an exemption by name and path only after seeing them.
